name: Blindsee Biberwier
kurzbeschreibung: The Blindsee near Biberwier at 1,093 m on the Fernpass: turquoise-blue high-alpine lake with a sunken forest, diving eldorado, and Zugspitze views.
beschreibung:
Overview

The captivating Blindsee sits at an altitude of 1,093 meters below the Fernpass summit in the Tyrolean municipality of Biberwier in the Reutte district (Außerfern). Cradled by dense mixed mountain forests at the foot of the imposing Mieminger Kette and commanding direct vistas of the Wettersteingebirge and the striking Zugspitze, this roughly 0.22-square-kilometer lake ranks among North Tyrol's most scenically stunning alpine gems. Reaching depths of up to 25 meters with visibility extending up to 15 meters, the lake enchants visitors with its luminous, almost Caribbean turquoise-blue hues.

Natural Phenomenon & Diving Paradise

Geologically, the lake was formed roughly 4,000 years ago by the massive Fernpass-Bergsturz (rockslide), which dammed the valley and impounded the water. The Blindsee owes its name to the fact that it possesses neither an above-ground inlet nor an outlet: it is nourished exclusively by subterranean karst aquifers and springs, with water seeping through porous rockslide debris toward the Loisachtal. The lake enjoys international acclaim among scuba divers: in 1984, a massive landslide triggered a sunken forest, sending hundreds of tree trunks plunging to the lakebed like giant pick-up sticks. The crystal-clear alpine water preserved the timber, allowing divers today to navigate a hauntingly beautiful underwater labyrinth populated by trophy lake trout, pike, and char (diving is permitted with a permit). For hikers, the roughly 5.5-kilometer Blindsee-Rundweg circumscribes the lake in about 1.5 to 2 hours. Along the northern shoreline, idyllic natural beaches and sunny rocky coves beckon visitors to swim and relax.

Visit & Getting There

The Blindsee and its circular trail are freely open and free of charge during snow-free months (approx. May through October/November). By car: via the B179 (Fernpassstraße) from Reutte or Nassereith to the Fernpass summit near the hotel Mohr Life Resort and Restaurant Fernpassblick; from there, a narrow, tolled private road (barrier gate, access toll approx. €8.00 per car) leads down to the lakeside parking area. Alternatively, visitors can park atop the Fernpass and hike down to the water along a forested trail in about 30 minutes. By public transport: ÖBB train to Lermoos or Ehrwald station, then Postbus line 150 to the stop Biberwier Fernpasshöhe, followed by a walk down to the lake.

Tips

Along the southern shore, the loop path traverses natural forest trails with exposed roots requiring sturdy footwear; the flatter northern bank offers a wider, gentler path. The renowned viewpoint along the Fernpassstraße (Fotopoint Blindsee) provides the most breathtaking photographic vantage point of the vibrant turquoise waters framed by the monumental Zugspitzmassiv.
